name: Coldblooded Kain Threat
notes: He wrestled for Professional World Wrestling, where Chris Williams was an executive and whose television championship was named for him: the federation's own broadcast of 21 January 1999 stages him with America's Most Wanted, alongside Congo and Northern Touch, in three segments and no match. Jay Phoenix remembered him as the federation's Television Champion, the man who held a terrified rookie to a twenty-minute draw and then hit him with the belt on the way out. eWNews named him too, in its own account of the fourth Chris Williams Memorial Cup (8 December 2003, /promotions/ew-news-2002/news/chris-williams-memorial-cup-2003-12-08.html): the Cup was held "to honour the memory of Chris Williams, better known as ‘Kain Threat’ of the PWW, who was killed in a car accident in 1999."
caption: The character behind the annual Chris Williams Memorial Cup — the hobby's own way of keeping his name spoken.

tenures.role: wrestler — one of the three men of America's Most Wanted, the stable Dr. Moreau led to the ring, with Congo and Northern Touch
tenures.source: The federation's own Wednesday Night Wildfire broadcast of 21 January 1999 (/promotions/pww-worldwide-1999/archive/pww-wednesday-night-wildfire-1999-01-21.html), from the 1999 RSPWF walk corpus, accession 0148. The undated draw is from Jay Phoenix's own roleplay "No More Tears" (phoenix.rpcommunity.com, captured 10 June 2004; the same piece posted to rpcommunity.com's own Quill forum, captured 18 July 2004; rpcommunity mine).
tenures.note: The federation's own broadcast books him in no match and stages him three times. First in the brawl that had spilled past the previous week's show going off the air, replayed to open this one: he hits the ring alongside Congo, takes a beating from Mav Richards and the Assassin, then holds his own manager back from Johnny Blaze and is led to the back with the rest of the stable. Then at the foot of the ramp with them, watching the opening contest that decided the stable's fourth member. Then in the ring afterwards, looking the winner over and walking out with him. The crowd's own signs read "AMW, the 3 baddest men on the planet." The commentary places a tag team of his with Army of One before an earlier closure of the federation, so he was in it before this card; the broadcast gives him no billing line, no vitals and no hometown. First and last seen are the one dated document's own date. Undated beside it: Jay Phoenix's own roleplay remembers wrestling him to a twenty-minute time-limit draw in Phoenix's first match for the federation, when Kain Threat was its Television Champion and had held the belt for months, and being clocked with that belt on the way out of the ring.

identity.note: The wrestler Professional World Wrestling billed as "Kain Threat" on its own broadcast of 21 January 1999 is this character. What holds it together: the federation is the one Chris Williams belonged to — GIWF's own broadcast of 18 April 2001 calls him a "former PWW Executive" — and it is the federation whose television championship carries his name; Jay Phoenix's own roleplay remembers Kain Threat as that television champion, holding the belt for months; the broadcast falls less than four months before his death; and no other character on the register carries both "Kain" and "Threat." What the record still does not have: the broadcast never says "Coldblooded," and nothing held names the character and the man who handled him in the same document.
